title: The reconciliation_result owner, the ACE product code, the reconciliation operation and the wave 3 harness pack are not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 R7.2 and R9; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 17, 41 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13, 14 and 15; legacy RWB-E4-050 sections 5, 8, 9, 12 and 15; Ownership Map entries reconciliation_result, proceeds, write_off, decision_log_entry and rule_row
section: 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.7 Tables owned; 12.8 Contract fakes; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states
description: Seven sets of values the story needs are given nowhere in the sources read. First, the ownership of reconciliation_result and the operation that reads it: the legacy key writes the outcome row inside module P8 Payments and posting, while the Ownership Map records reconciliation_result under P1 rwb-source-data (Architecture v5 slide 41 reconciliation, slide 44 JOB-04 owner rwb-source-data), and no source read names the operation that lists the rows for a rec_code and a business date, the field names those rows carry or the result codes they take. Second, the data product code that serves the v_ace_payment, v_ace_write_off and v_ace_batch_status rows through GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/{productCode}/records. Third, the reconciliation operation and its field names: the identifier in the run environment that resolves to JOB-04 for the rerun path, and the business facts the owner records for each rule. Fourth, the rule set behind the loop: REC-04 and REC-06 are named only in legacy RWB-E4-050 and no rule set read defines them or names the package that carries them, while REC-05 is the P1 reconciliation duty over the ACE views, so the rule IDs and versions the decision record must cite are unnamed. Fifth, the read of the approved write-off: the operation in rwb-writeoff and the field names that carry the write-off key, the amount, the posting date and the approval. Sixth, the result codes and the tolerance behind the reconciliation, which no source read in this WP names. Seventh, the wave 3 harness pack: the SIT environment specification, the seeding set and its fixtures for account A-0001, the evidence report format and its retention, and the feature flag key of the harness. Every one of these is written with the section R9 placeholder in the story rather than invented.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 gives the P1 row owns ACE view contract, extension tables, freshness and reconciliation with schema rwb_source_data, slide 15 gives P1 IN REST GET /freshness and POST /business-days/{date}/ready (Airflow) with the fallback that polls the ACE batch record and TMP Workflow: AceIngestCheck, reconciliation, and gives P1 OUT DB schema rwb_source_data with no table or operation named, slide 44 gives JOB-04 Reconciliation as an event-triggered workflow in rwb-source-data started by AceDataReady, and slide 17 gives P8 IN REST GET /cases/{id}/payments and POST /proceeds/{id}/allocate, TMP Act matchPayments and confirmBookings, and P8 OUT DB schema rwb_payment: payment and proceeds matching, fees, bookings, posting files, with no reconciliation operation and no reconciliation_result table named. Legacy RWB-E4-050 names module P8 Payments and posting, states Endpoints: None with the work running as a service or a scheduled job inside the recovery module, and its AC1 names REC-04, REC-06 and REC-05, reconciliation_result by rec_code and business date, and v_ace_payment, v_ace_write_off and v_ace_batch_status, without a table owner, an operation or a field name. Ownership Map records reconciliation_result under P1, proceeds under P8, write_off under S7, decision_log_entry and rule_row under P7, and carries operations GET /admin/jobs and POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun under P1 with no reconciliation_result read path. Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13 to 15 give the four steps receive, ask, record and apply and the rule package governance without naming REC-04 or REC-06. Business Requirements Program v4 carries REQ-RDF-007, REQ-RDF-008, REQ-CHO-009, REQ-S7-005 and REQ-DRI-001 without a product code, a package code or a result code.
proposed: Settle at the wave 3 entry check, with the integration lead, the QA lead, the data product owner and the P1 and P8 owners, that reconciliation_result and its rec_code and business date belong to P1 rwb-source-data and are read only through its contract, name that read operation and its result codes, name the data product code for the three ACE views, name the job identifier for JOB-04, name the package and rule IDs behind REC-04, REC-05 and REC-06, name the rwb-writeoff read operation and its fields, and agree the wave 3 harness pack with its environment, seeding set, evidence format and retention.

title: The split of the legacy instruction step, the instruction and pack field names, and which clock is the partner clock
source: Legacy RWB-E5-009; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 17, 19 and 25; Ownership Map v1; API Specification v4; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; Event and Messaging Design v4
description: The legacy step ran inside one module: one component issued the instruction, sent the pack, started the partner clock and wrote the record. In the target the pack is P5 rwb-document with its serving fact P6 rwb-comms, the instruction and result are S9 rwb-partner, the panel evaluation and the case move are S4 rwb-litigation, and the partner clock is P3 rwb-case, and no source read states the order of those four, which one compensates when a later hop fails, or what the harness should assert when only the first three succeed. The same missing detail covers: the request and response fields of the instruction operation and of the result path; the field of partner_instruction that carries the pack reference; the fields of partner that carry the court region, the case type and the conflict-check outcome that R-LIT-24 conditions the instruction on; the timer type, the start value and the due date the partner clock is measured from, and whether the partner clock is P3 CaseWorkflow durable timer or the S9 InstructionWorkflow SLA timer, since both are in the sources; the idempotency key of the instruction operation that R-UNI-40 needs; the surface that serves the pack to a law firm, being a P5 document link or a P6 notice or message, and whether a notice to a law firm is in P6 scope at all; whether MSG-S4-001 is raised at the instruction or only at filing; the harness environment, seeding set, pack fixture, evidence report format and retention, and the feature flag key; and which owner fixes an incomplete pack, since pack assembly belongs to RWB-S4-E5009-APP and P5 while the harness only reads it.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E5-009 data, endpoints and test cases; Architecture v5 slide 16 (rwb-document: metadata, custody, OCR, signatures, retention), slide 17 (rwb-comms notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery; rwb-partner panel, partner users, instructions, results with InstructionWorkflow SLA timers), slide 19 (rwb-litigation legal actions, hearings, judgments, enforcement and only LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded and AuctionResult), slide 25 (CaseWorkflow and its long timers); Ownership Map v1 POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions, GET /partner/instructions, POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results, GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}, GET /cases/{caseId}/timers; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-LIT-09; R-LIT-24, R-LIT-26, R-UNI-39, R-UNI-40 and R-UNI-45; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-20 InstructionIssued
proposed: At the wave 3 entry check confirm four things and close this gap: the four owners and the order of the instruction, the pack, the case move and the timer, with the rule for a partial step; the S9 instruction and result contract with its field names, its pack reference and its idempotency key when the rwb-partner CON story publishes it; which timer is the partner clock with its timer type and due date source; and the surface that serves the pack, being a P5 link or a P6 notice. Until then the harness asserts the chain through the owners contracts with the defaults in ASM-B-ITG-W3-02-E5009-1 to -5.

title: Wave 3 journey harness pack, seeded identifiers, fixed business date, product codes, unnamed operations, evidence format and gate thresholds are not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 R7.2 and R9; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41, 42, 43, 44 and 46; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 17 to 21; legacy RWB-E4-001, RWB-E4-002, RWB-E4-045, RWB-E4-046, RWB-E4-047, RWB-E4-050, RWB-E5-002 and RWB-E5-009; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.8 Contract fakes; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states; 16 Test cases
description: W3J01 is a new story with no legacy counterpart, so every harness value it needs is new and seven sets of values are given nowhere in the sources read. First, the harness environment: its repository, deployment, namespace and pipeline. Second, the seeded case and every identifier on it, namely the case and its route, its asset and appraisal beyond the values the legacy keys state, its payment and proceeds, its treatment beyond treatment T-0001, its guarantee, its notice and its partner. Third, the business date the wave 3 journey runs for, which no source names for a journey; the story fixes 2026-12-14 because the legacy reconciliation key RWB-E4-050 names that ACE batch date. Fourth, the evidence report format, its retention and the wave gate definition with its name and its thresholds beyond all green. Fifth, the operation names no source gives: the write that records the proof of delivery on a notice, the read of the JOB-04 reconciliation outcome, and the read of a guarantee claim, since the ownership map gives P6 GET /notices/{noticeId} with the proof of delivery on the answer and no delivery-confirmation path, gives S3 POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims and PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId} and no claim read path, and gives rwb-source-data no reconciliation read path. Sixth, the data product code behind each product read, for v_ace_valuation, valuation_ext, v_ace_payment, v_ace_write_off, v_ace_batch_status and v_ace_account, and the row of reconciliation_result that carries each count. Seventh, the wave 3 harness pack itself: its fixed seeding set and fixtures, and how the eight harness stories of the wave share one gate. No source read gives any of these values, so each is written with the section R9 placeholder in the story and the harness is configured from the assumptions below.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R7.2 (section 12 tables and section 16 levels) and R9 (placeholder and candidate rows); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (service catalogue with no harness environment, no product code and no reconciliation path), slide 42 and slide 43 (event catalogue: NoticeDelivered, InstructionIssued and DecisionRecorded, with no product code), slide 44 (JOB-04 Reconciliation owned by rwb-source-data as an event-triggered workflow, and JOB-10 WIN notices at 16:00) and slide 46 (contract tests per API, event and activity, Temporal replay tests and a daily journey smoke workflow, with no evidence format and no threshold); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 17 (RouteDecisionWorkflow and the 12-month appraisal clock), slide 19 (GuaranteeClaimWorkflow and the claim deadline), slide 20 (LitigationWorkflow, the notice period and the instruction) and slide 21; legacy RWB-E4-050 (v_ace_payment, v_ace_write_off, v_ace_batch_status, REC-04, REC-05 and REC-06, ACE batch date 2026-12-14 and reconciliation_result by rec_code and business date), RWB-E4-002 (appraisal AP-0001 for asset AST-0001 at appraisal date 2026-11-02 with appraised value 4250000), RWB-E4-046 (treatment T-0001 at 820000 for account A-0001), RWB-E5-002 (notice, proof window of 7 days, NOTICE_DISPATCHED to WITH_CUSTOMER_NOTICE_PERIOD) and RWB-E5-009 (partner instruction and partner clock); ownership.json (GET /notices/{noticeId} P6, POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims and PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId} S3, reconciliation_result P1, and no reconciliation read path).
proposed: Agree at the wave 3 entry check, with the integration and QA leads, the harness environment and pipeline, the fixed seeding set and its fixtures, the business date and the ACE batch used, the data product code behind each product read, the evidence report format and its retention, the gate name and its thresholds, and how the eight wave 3 harness stories share one gate. Settle the three unnamed operations with their owners: the P6 delivery-confirmation operation, the P1 reconciliation read and the S3 claim read, or confirm that the P6 notice read, the P1 product records and the S3 create answer are the only reads the run needs. Record each value in the wave 3 harness pack, and cite the gap in the evidence report until it is closed.

title: The legacy delivery step is split across rwb-comms, rwb-litigation and rwb-case with no named hand-off operation and no named reference rows, so the end-to-end chain of RWB-E5-002 has no single source of record
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-002); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 17, 19, 14, 41, 42, 43); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slide 7); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.2); Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (A2.1.1 measure); Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 (API-P6-001 to API-P6-011, notice fields); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (API-S4-001 to API-S4-005, R-LIT-07 to R-LIT-09); Recovery Workbench TSD P3 Case and workflow v3; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023, DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023, DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (row FEAT-LIT-02); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09, R-UNI-39, R-UNI-40); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 (sections 5.3, 5.6, 5.7, 5.11); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (notice, template and merge_field own P6; legal_action and hearing own S4; recovery_case, timer and task own P3; decision_log_entry and rule_row own P7)
section: 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 4, 5, 6, 9, 11; 7 Acceptance criteria; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.2; 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 18 Traceability
description: The legacy key RWB-E5-002 is one in-process step: the delivery confirmation is written onto the case, the notice period starts from the delivered date (R-LIT-07), an expired proof window marks the notice unserved and starts no period (R-LIT-08), and a failed decision log write blocks the whole action (R-UNI-39). In the target that step is split across three owners and every part of the split is open. (1) The delivery fact is a fact of the notice and belongs to rwb-comms, which owns notices, templates, merge fields and proof of delivery (Architecture v5 slide 41 and slide 17; ownership map notice, template and merge_field own P6); the evaluation of R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 and the legal action belong to rwb-litigation (slide 41 and slide 19; legal_action and hearing own S4); the case route move, the notice-period timer and its task belong to rwb-case (slide 14 and slide 41; recovery_case, timer and task own P3). No source describes the delivered chain as one operation, and no source names the operation that carries the delivery fact from the notice to the litigation evaluation, although the two sibling slices build against a contract they call RWB-S4-E5002-CON. (2) The proof-record operation name on that S4 contract is not named by any source: the TSD S4 appendix T-A ends at API-S4-001 to API-S4-005 (notice approve, legal action create, read, patch, hearings) and none of them records a proof of delivery. (3) The notice proof write path that the P6 slice designs, POST /notices/{noticeId}/proof-of-delivery, is also not named by a source: the TSD P6 appendix T-A ends at API-P6-011 and none of the eleven operations records a proof. (4) The mapping of a LOV-DELIVERY value onto the notice state is not stated by any source read: LOV-DELIVERY exists with DELIVERED, REFUSED, UNDELIVERABLE and PENDING (DF-LEG-022), and the SCR-18 list names the states generated, approved, sent, delivered and unserved, but which value produces which state, and what PENDING means for the notice, is not written down. (5) The notice row of the LDM carries nine fields, DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023, and none of them is a lifecycle state, so the Delivered and Unserved state the screens show is a standard column of the P6 TSD design and has no field ID. (6) The notice-period duration, its reference row code and value, and the proof window length that R-LIT-08 and the Temporal design carry, are data of the business that no source read names as rows. (7) The three case facts the P3 slice adds for this step, the notice reference, the delivered date and the outcome, have no field ID either, and the case row they sit on is recovery_case, DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023. (8) The sources conflict on how the proof arrives: the Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 describes FEAT-LIT-02 as running unattended and reading v_ace_pod, which is the Epic 2 WIN proof loop, while the legacy story master is officer-driven and R-LIT-08 marks a notice unserved when the proof window expires; the automatic loop is the P6 Epic 2 story RWB-P6-E2021-APP and is proven by RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG, and this chain starts from a notice already Sent. (9) The hand-off direction between rwb-litigation and rwb-case is not fixed by any source: whether the case reads the litigation answer or is signalled by it is the P3 slice design, and only the outcome is provable from outside. (10) The harness pack is open end to end: the environment, the seeding set, the fixture contents, the evidence format and its retention, and the feature-flag keys are not specified. (11) The legacy story master carries no requirement ID and the EP05 PRD is pending (C1), so the trace of this chain runs to the Program BRD requirements it serves and not to an ID of its own. (12) The litigation rule package code that carries R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 is not named by any source read; only the version in force per environment is knowable, from the rwb-decision registry.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 17 (P6 IN: POST /notices, GET /cases/{id}/notices; OUT: rwb_comms with notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery; rwb.comms.events.v1 NoticeGenerated, NoticeDispatched, NoticeDelivered), slide 19 (S4 IN: GET/POST /legal-actions, GET/POST /hearings, event NoticeDelivered; OUT: rwb_litigation, LitigationWorkflow, partner issueInstruction and comms child demand notice), slide 14 (P3 IN: GET /cases/{id}, GET /tasks; OUT: rwb_case case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation, timers; CaseWorkflow parent), slide 41 (the 19-service catalogue rows for P3, P6 and S4), slide 42 rows 13 to 15 (NoticeGenerated, NoticeDispatched, NoticeDelivered; NoticeDelivered consumed by rwb-litigation, rwb-guarantee and rwb-case) and row 08 (DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1); Temporal and Drools design slide 7 (proof of delivery EV-15 starts the notice-period timer, R-LIT-07, proof window 7 days); TSD P6 T-A API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 with no proof operation; TSD S4 T-A API-S4-001 to API-S4-005 with no proof operation and the rule table R-LIT-07 to R-LIT-09; LDM v8 DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023 (nine notice fields, delivery_status on LOV-DELIVERY, callback_date, barcode, sent_date) and DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 (timer_type, started_at, expires_at, status); Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-LIT-02 (reads the WIN proof of delivery from v_ace_pod, runs unattended) against the legacy story master RWB-E5-002 (As a litigation officer, I want the Workbench to write the delivery confirmation onto the case); FSD S4 A2.2 rule table; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09, R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-40; ownership map notice, template, merge_field, legal_action, hearing, recovery_case, timer and task; DP-01, DP-05, DP-13, DP-19.
area: Service contracts; Case and workflow state; Reference data; Test harness
proposed: Publish the proof-record operation on RWB-S4-E5002-CON and the notice proof write on the rwb-comms baseline, with their paths, request and answer shapes and error envelopes; add the notice lifecycle state and the three case notice facts to the LDM with field IDs; fix the LOV-DELIVERY to notice-state mapping and the notice-period duration and proof window as versioned reference rows with their codes; record in the P6 and S4 appendices that the automatic v_ace_pod loop is the Epic 2 dispatch story and not this step; and let the EP05 PRD attach the requirement ID to FEAT-LIT-02. Until then this harness asserts the owners published answers, reads the reference rows at their versions and cites this row.
